info.bio: Hubo un tiempo, en Berlín (muy) a principios de los noventa, cuando la música de baile electrónica había llegado a su primera madurez y se había transformado en «El sonido de la ciudad de las mil músicas». Siendo el lugar que es, ya se habían realizado serias teorizaciones formales y filosóficas sobre el fenómeno techno y cualquiera con un poco de interés podía haberse enterado por Frank Hartmann de que la repetición del bucle rítmico significa una quiebra con el pensamiento estético kantiano.

own_scenes.family: Segunda ola de Detroit: UR, Plus 8, Carl Craig
own_scenes.desc: Para algunos, ir al underground significaba atrincherarse: UR nació del encuentro, en 1989 en los estudios United Sound, de un ex músico de sesión, Mike Banks (guitarrista de los Mechanics y de Members of the House), y Jeff Mills, que venía del industrial. Ignorados por Metroplex como Plus 8 por Transmat, grababan gratis a cambio de limpiar el estudio de Don Davis y en el Traxx de Ted Dudley. Fusionaron Members of the House y The Final Cut: «The Theory» y el tema con Yolanda (1990) eran casi tan radiables como Inner City, pero con «Waveform» (1991), editado en etiqueta negra frente a las blancas, encontraron su identidad: casi sin entrevistas, mensajes grabados en los surcos, estética militar (el padre de Banks y su mentor T. G. Williams, veterano de Vietnam), comparados con Public Enemy. En directo, Mills a los platos, Banks enmascarado con un pañuelo, D-Ha a los teclados y Robert Hood con máscara de gas. Rechazaron a Mute (solo cedieron «Elimination» a Paroxysm) y a las multinacionales: «somos un sello». «The Punisher» (1991), abrasiva, dio a Europa el castigo que pedía, y tras la gira la serie World Power Alliance (1992) elevó a UR a mito. Los proyectos X-101 y X-102 lanzaron Tresor; en el año 2000 pelearon con Sony, que hizo una copia nota por nota de «Jaguar» de DJ Rolando. «Es una guerra por el alma que empezó mucho antes que UR».

refs.q: Apparently as early as 1991, UR had sensed that the African American component of techno music was under siege.
refs.para: That release turned out to be 1991’s “Waveform,” a record that quickly manifested UR’s identity. The group made its first statement by rejecting the “white label” releases common at the time, instead releasing “Wave-form” as a black label—perhaps an early reaction against white techno artists, spurred by Plus 8’s entrance onto the scene and, more probably, the increasing influence of the European market. Apparently as early as 1991, UR had sensed that the African American component of techno music was under siege.
refs.chapter: Cap. 5: Off to Battle: Redefining the Detroit Underground, 1990–1995

refs.q: Here it’s like Vietnam—I’m not getting close to anybody.”
refs.para: But if UR’s sound was aggressive, its attitude was marked more by caution and protection of its own turf and the Detroit techno sound in general. “There’s a very strong, individualistic mentality here in Detroit,” said Banks in 1992. “You develop it without even noticing. I didn’t notice it until I went overseas, where everyone has several real close, dear friends. Here it’s like Vietnam—I’m not getting close to anybody.”
refs.chapter: Cap. 5: Off to Battle: Redefining the Detroit Underground, 1990–1995

refs.q: Jeff told him, “No, we’re a record label.”
refs.para: We had a college kid call us from a major [label], saying, “[Are] you guys looking to get a deal?” Jeff told him, “No, we’re a record label.” Then the kid says [sarcastically], “I know. I know, but do you want a deal?” [Banks laughs.] A real ass-hole! These labels just don’t understand that there’s a whole generation of people out here that are tired of being prostituted by major record companies. They [the majors] are real frustrated that basement labels are placing way higher in the charts than they do.
refs.chapter: Cap. 5: Off to Battle: Redefining the Detroit Underground, 1990–1995

refs.q: We await our next challenger, because for us it’s a forever war and not a war for fame, fortune, or females—it’s a war for soul that started long before UR. We are an electronic continuation of it.”
refs.para: Explains Hawtin, “Everyone had that kind of mentality and philosophy about going against the industry. We were all fighting the battle of distribution and getting things out there.” Adds Banks, “In retrospect, those were some great times with Plus 8. In fact, we still laugh about [those days] now. Unfortunately, no one has stepped up into the ring quite like Plus 8 used to. We await our next challenger, because for us it’s a forever war and not a war for fame, fortune, or females—it’s a war for soul that started long before UR. We are an electronic continuation of it.”

podcast.title: Formation and Philosophy (1989)
podcast.body: Underground Resistance emerged in 1989 as part of the second wave of techno. This collective of DJs and producers formed with the explicit goal of reclaiming the essential, underground spirit of Detroit techno, reacting against its commercialization by multinational corporations. "En 1989 aparece Ander Grand Resistans... quieren retomar la esencia en derrándole de Detroit."

srcs.episode: La historia del TECHNO en DETROIT. Cómo la música salvó a una ciudad atrapada

podcast.title: Anonymous Image and Sound
podcast.body: Members of Underground Resistance were known for performing camouflaged, maintaining anonymity. They developed a very minimalist, pure, and dense techno sound, distinct from the earlier, more house-like techno, focusing heavily on rhythmic bases. "underground resistans no se sabía quienes eran por que iban camuflados y cogen ese sonido techno que antes era tan parecido a música Houting y lo convierte un sonido muy minimalista, muy puro y muy denso."

srcs.episode: La historia del TECHNO en DETROIT. Cómo la música salvó a una ciudad atrapada

podcast.title: Collective and Evolving Entity
podcast.body: Underground Resistance is described as a "meta-group" or an independent philosophy rather than a fixed band. People have continuously joined and left, making it an evolving entity where no single individual embodies Underground Resistance. "nadie en concreto es underground resistans, underground resistans es una filosofía independiente de entender el techno."

srcs.episode: La historia del TECHNO en DETROIT. Cómo la música salvó a una ciudad atrapada

podcast.title: Early Techno Records as Cult Objects
podcast.body: The early records by groups like Socomo Anderran resistan, which emerged from the Detroit techno scene, are now regarded as genuine cult items. This is despite initial critiques that characterized early techno as uncreative, monotonous, and repetitive. "hoy en día los discos los primeros discos en música tecno de grupos pues como Juanáxia y Socomo Anderran resistan son auténticos objetos de culto."

srcs.episode: EL TRAP SÍ ES MÚSICA. (Aunque a lo mejor no te guste)

podcast.title: Influence on Modern Techno
podcast.body: Along with Richie Hawtin, Underground Resistance is largely responsible for creating the minimalist, rhythm-heavy, monotonous, and constant techno sound that is known today, often without melody. This sound is considered more characteristic of the second wave of techno than the initial creations of the genre's founders. "la segunda gran generación del techno, creo el techno que conocemos hoy en día, el techno minimalista, cargadísimo de base rímpica, monótono, constante, donde la melodía a veces ya ni siquiera existe."

srcs.episode: La historia del TECHNO en DETROIT. Cómo la música salvó a una ciudad atrapada

podcast.title: Social and Political Activism
podcast.body: Underground Resistance was deeply committed to its underground philosophy, linking with African-American liberation movements and anti-capitalist urban guerrilla movements. This commitment reflected their desire to return to the primal philosophy of techno, where people without resources united in trance states through rhythmic bases. "Underground resistans estaba tan concienciado con la filosofía underground que estuvo vinculado por ejemplo en los movimientos de liberación afraamericanos, a movimientos de guerrilla orban antica pitalista."
